sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 12.8% a year from $4.86 billion in FY2016 to $14.3 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F198].
The path was a step change, not a smooth climb: revenue jumped 89.1% in FY2021 to $16.1 billion, then fell 24.3% in FY2022 to $12.2 billion [D241][F6][D292][F7].
REGEN-COV contributed 66.4pp of FY2021 growth and 36.3pp of the FY2022 decline [D582][D585].
Since FY2022 revenue has grown at a 5.6% three-year CAGR while operating income fell at 8.9% a year, and operating margin has declined four straight years to 24.9% [D767][D769][R1][F30].
In FY2025 collaboration revenue contributed 9.0pp of the 1.0% revenue growth, while net product sales subtracted 9.3pp [D523][D440][D507].
Regeneron's share of Sanofi antibody profits added 9.3pp and reached 36.5% of revenue, the largest single driver [D592][D590].
That share rose on higher Dupixent profits, while the Bayer share of EYLEA profits fell 8.6% on lower ex-US EYLEA sales [P9][D731][P8].
US EYLEA sales fell 42.4% and subtracted 14.2pp, on competitive pressure, compounded bevacizumab and the EYLEA HD transition [D577][D578][P10].
Operating costs grew 4.4pp faster than revenue in FY2025, at 5.4%, so operating income fell 10.3% [D464][D457][D441].
Operating margin of 24.9% is the window low, below the 34.6% median and far below the 55.7% FY2021 high [F30][D749][D751][D750].
In FY2025 R&D took 4.7pp of margin and SG&A gave back 2.0pp, for a net 3.2pp decline [D465][D466][D453].
SG&A fell 8.6% mainly on lower charitable contributions to Good Days, partly offset by about $60 million of fourth-quarter matching donations [D456][P5].
Net margin of 31.4% sat 6.5pp above the 24.9% operating margin, as other income of $1.65 billion and a 13.9% tax rate lifted the bottom line [F50][F30][D797][X117][D427].
Operating cash flow of $4.98 billion was 1.11x net income, above the 1.10x window median, and free cash flow was 0.91x [F80][D428][D787][D429].
Free cash flow margin of 28.4% is above the 26.4% window median and the 22.0% peer median [D425][D757][D777].
Capex of $898 million was 6.3% of revenue and 1.65x D&A, the highest capex since FY2020 [F90][D424][D430].
Stock-based compensation of $994 million equalled 20.0% of operating cash flow [X77][D431].
Net cash of $16.9 billion is 117.7% of revenue, in the 100th percentile of eight biopharma peers against a -50.7% median [D434][D435][D780][D781].
Debt is a flat $1.99 billion against $18.9 billion of cash and investments, and the current ratio is 4.13x [F187][D432][F180].
Buybacks plus dividends of $3.81 billion were 93.3% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count fell 5.6% [D436][D437][D459].
The balance sheet is a large cushion, but return on average equity of 14.9% trails the 38.7% peer median [D439][D785].
Operating margin has fallen four years running, from 55.7% in FY2021 to 24.9% in FY2025, a 30.7pp decline [R1][F26][F30].
The decline reflects a mix shift toward lower-margin collaboration profit shares and rising R&D, so the FY2021 level looks unrepeatable [D590][D420].
FY2018 and FY2019 revenue in the table are later recasts: $5.15 billion versus $6.71 billion first reported, and $6.56 billion versus $7.86 billion [R2][F3][X3][F4][X4].
Growth and margins spanning those years mix two presentations, so the FY2018 decline and FY2019 rebound should not be read at face value [D92][D143].
Whether US EYLEA sales, $2.75 billion in FY2025, stabilize or fall further in the FY2026 10-K [S43].
Whether operating margin holds above the 24.9% window low or breaks it in FY2026 [F30][D749].
Whether R&D as a share of revenue, 40.8% in FY2025, keeps climbing toward the 42.2% window high [D420][D759].
